def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (K F : Fm → Fm) (conF : Fm),
    𝓢 ⊢ K conF 🡒 conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ K (∼conF) 🡒 ∼conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ K conF 🡒 F conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ conF 🡒 ∼F conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF ⋏ (conF 🡒 ∼K (∼conF))
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, given implication, conjunction, disjunction, negation, truth and falsehood on Fm and a provability relation for systems in S, take any system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K and F from Fm to Fm and every sentence c (the parameter conF), if 𝓢 proves each of (1) K(c) → c, (2) K(¬c) → ¬c, (3) K(c) → F(c), and (4) c → ¬F(c), then 𝓢 proves the single conjunction ¬K(c) ∧ (c → ¬K(¬c)). The second conjunct is conditional on c, not an unconditional negation of K(¬c). No consistency assumption on 𝓢, rule taking a proof of φ to a proof of K(φ), or interpretation of c as a consistency sentence for F is required."}
translation: Target is the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, given implication, conjunction, disjunction, negation, truth and falsehood on Fm and a provability relation for systems in S, take any system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K and F from Fm to Fm and every sentence c (the parameter conF), if 𝓢 proves each of (1) K(c) → c, (2) K(¬c) → ¬c, (3) K(c) → F(c), and (4) c → ¬F(c), then 𝓢 proves the single conjunction ¬K(c) ∧ (c → ¬K(¬c)). The second conjunct is conditional on c, not an unconditional negation of K(¬c). No consistency assumption on 𝓢, rule taking a proof of φ to a proof of K(φ), or interpretation of c as a consistency sentence for F is required.

judgement.summary: With `conF` standing for `ConsF`, the stated repair assumes the two K-correctness instances, the local inclusion, and the second-incompleteness implication, and concludes that 𝓢 proves `¬K(ConsF) ∧ (ConsF → ¬K(¬ConsF))`. Only the second conjunct is conditional on consistency; the printed corollary’s existential hypothesis is neither assumed nor used to infer the local inclusion.
